title: RBAC v2 drift detection and SSO assertion replay mitigation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Implement automated detection for RBAC v2 policy drift and harden SSO/SAML processing to mitigate assertion replay and related admin path attacks. This ticket bundles: a drift detection pipeline and alerting, assertion nonce/ttl enforcement and token binding add-ons, expanded audit events for admin privilege grants and session fingerprints, and remediation items surfaced by the latest penetration test.

Background: During the 2026 Q1 pentest (see links) the red team demonstrated two recurring weaknesses: (1) stale RBAC policy artifacts and out-of-band role changes (drift) that allowed privilege escalation between deploy cycles, and (2) an SSO assertion replay scenario against secondary admin endpoints where assertion reuse could extend privileges for short windows. Current RBAC v2 supports rich role expressions and delegation; however, we lack a reliable externalized drift detection to alert on changes that grant additional privileges, and our SAML processing accepts assertions without a short-lived nonce cache for admin-level flows.

Goals:
- Ship an RBAC-drift detector that ingests policy snapshots and detects privilege expansion vectors (new grants, broadened resource globs, added bypass rules) and generates actionable alerts for oncall and product security.
- Enforce SAML assertion replay protection for admin flows: add nonce/ID cache with TTL, strict audience checks, and optional token binding (if client supports).
- Expand audit events: admin-privilege-eval, rbac-policy-change(diff), saml-assertion-verified, saml-assertion-replay-detected, admin-session-fingerprint. Events must include minimal identifying metadata (actor id, session id, assertion id, policy-version) and be forwarded to existing telemetry pipeline.
- Implement automated remediation playbook stubs for high-risk drift alerts (e.g., auto-rollback of recent policy change + create incident room).

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope includes hosted and Dedicated control planes; Private (on-prem) packaging to be covered by separate follow-up but audit schema must be compatible. Not covering rebuilding complete RBAC policy editor (UI work will be a separate PM ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Drift detector runs on policy snapshots (cron + on-change hook) and produces structured alerts into Slack + security queue with a reproducible diff and suggested rollback link.
2) SAML assertion replay attempts are detected and rejected for admin-scoped assertions; rejection increments a counter and emits a saml-assertion-replay-detected audit event.
3) New audit events are stored in our audit index schema and appear in the Console’s admin activity timeline for at least 90 days (configurable).
4) Unit and integration tests cover edge cases: out-of-order policy merges, overlapping role definitions, duplicate assertion IDs, clock skew up to 120s.
5) Performance: additional SAML checks add <2ms median latency on auth path under normal load (measured via canary).

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Design & threat modeling (completed) — produce schema for drift diffs, list of privilege expansion heuristics, and SAML nonce cache design.
- Week 2: Implement RBAC snapshot ingestor + diff engine; wire to alerting infra.
- Week 3: Implement SAML assertion nonce cache (in-memory with bounded size + persistent fallback via Redis for multi-node), audience + token-binding checks; add retry/backoff for clock skew.
- Week 4: Add audit event emission, Console wiring, and end-to-end tests; run canary.
- Rollout: Canary (10% control plane traffic) -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with automatic rollback on error budget breaches.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We chose a detection-first approach (alerts + manual rollback) rather than auto-remediation for all events to avoid risky automatic privilege removals. High confidence categories (e.g., exact parent policy revert) will have opt-in auto-rollback in a later iteration.
- Nonce cache will use a hybrid in-memory + Redis design to avoid single-node replay windows while keeping typical latency low. This increases operational complexity but is necessary for Dedicated clusters.
- Token binding will be optional and gated behind a feature flag; it requires client changes and longer rollout for customers on older SSO providers.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for diff rules and SAML validator.
- Integration test: simulate policy update stream, ensure drift alert threshold triggers.
- Pen-test re-run: coordinate with security to validate that replay scenario is mitigated (retest scheduled).
- Load test: measure auth path latency and Redis hit rates.

Monitoring & observability:
- Metrics: rbac_drift_alerts_total{severity=...}, saml_assertion_replays_detected_total, admin_audit_events_emitted_total, saml_nonce_cache_hit_rate.
- Alerts: P1 if saml_assertion_replays_detected_total > 5 in 5m for production control plane; P2 for drift_alerts_no_ack in 24h.

Rollback plan:
- Canary monitor integration with error budget; manual rollback flag available in control plane for policy evaluation service. If canary latency >2x baseline or error budget exceeded, revert to previous image and disable nonce enforcement temporarily (safe-fail to logging only).

Security and compliance notes:
- Security review required (see metadata). Cryptographic decisions (nonce generation, token binding) reviewed by crypto team.
- Audit event schema designed to satisfy audit retention requirements and legal eDiscovery for enterprise customers.

Deliverables:
- RBAC drift detector service + alerting playbook.
- SAML nonce cache + verifier changes in auth service.
- Audit event schema and Console timeline integration.
- Tests, canary, pen-test validation report.
